newsitem.title: UK: Optimism in UK financial services up sharply - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Optimism in UK financial services up sharply - CBI.

text.p: Optimism among UK financial services firms has risen sharply for the third quarter running, according to a survey by the Confederation of British Industry and Coopers & Lybrand.
Business confidence rose most among life insurers, finance houses and building societies, the survey showed. Only securities houses reported a drop in confidence in the third quarter of the year.
"Business confidence is growing strongly this year, with the volume of business and profitability picking up," said Sudhir Junankar, the CBI's associate director of economic analysis.
A positive balance of 46 percent of firms said they were more optimistic than three months ago.

"This recovery seems to be from a low base, with firms saying that their level of business is still a little below normal. But the bounceback in profits is becoming firmly established," Junankar said.
The volume of business is expected to increase over the next three months in all financial services sectors except securities traders and venture capitalists.

Pat Newberry, a senior member of the Coopers & Lybrand's consultancy, said the gloom among securities firms was based on a worry that the FTSE-100 index of leading UK shares may be due for a correction. The index broke above 4,000 for the first time on Wednesday, but many analysts are forecasting a fall soon.
The main constraint on business over the coming year is expected to be the level of demand, the survey showed.
Newberry said the insurance and building society sectors were still suffering from overcapacity, making further rationalisation inevitable.
Employment among financial services firms fell faster than expected in the third quarter and at the fastest rate since December.
Investment in information technology is expected to grow strongly over the coming year.

"As we expected in June, financial services have had a good summer, with customers buying more services," Newberry said. "The financial services market is still highly competitive, but companies are alive to this and are gearing the IT spending to meet the challenge."
The survey canvassed 292 financial services firms.
